answer_text:
There isn’t one single “best” website—it depends on what you’re buying (heavy strength gear vs. cardio vs. budget accessories). For most people building a solid home gym in the US, these are the best bets:

## Best overall for serious strength equipment: **Rogue Fitness**
Best for racks, barbells, plates, benches, and “buy-it-for-life” core pieces (especially if you’re building a garage gym). ([roguefitness.com](https://www.roguefitness.com/garage-gym?utm_source=openai))

## Best value + strong quality for home-gym builds: **REP Fitness**
Great for racks, benches, storage, and a lot of strength accessories—often a strong price-to-quality choice compared with premium brands. ([repfitness.com](https://repfitness.com/?utm_source=openai))

## Best for convenience, fast shipping, and easy returns: **Amazon**
Best when you want basics quickly (bands, adjustable dumbbells, mats, kettlebells, small accessories). Quality varies a lot by listing, so it’s better for “commodity” gear than a centerpiece rack/cable system. ([tomsguide.com](https://www.tomsguide.com/wellness/workouts/forget-costly-memberships-these-12-gym-essentials-will-help-you-work-out-at-home?utm_source=openai))

## Best if you want to see/try cardio locally (plus delivery/setup options): **Dick’s / local specialty dealers**
Often better for treadmills, bikes, ellipticals—things where comfort, noise, and service matter. ([plategym.com](https://plategym.com/home-gym-equipment-shops-online-vs-local-in-2026/?utm_source=openai))

### If you tell me:
1) your budget, 2) your space (apartment/garage), and 3) what you want (strength, cardio, or both),  
I’ll recommend the single best site (or 2-site combo) for your exact shopping list.
